title: How to Spot a Phishing Link
summary: Phishing links imitate a real service to trick you into entering credentials or approving a transaction. The address often looks almost right — a swapped letter, an extra word, or a lookalike domain ending.
blocks: Phishing links imitate a real service to trick you into entering credentials or approving a transaction. The address often looks almost right — a swapped letter, an extra word, or a lookalike domain ending.
Before you connect a wallet or sign in, read the full domain carefully, and reach sites through your own bookmark or a search rather than a link someone sent you.
Treat links in unexpected emails, DMs and ads as untrusted by default. The safest habit is to navigate to important sites yourself instead of clicking through.
